title: Comprehensive Outpatient Cardiac Rehabilitation
description: CMS National Coverage Determination for outpatient cardiac rehabilitation programs (NCD 20.10). Requires documented qualifying cardiac diagnosis: acute myocardial infarction within the preceding 12 months, CABG surgery, stable angina pectoris, heart valve repair/replacement, PCI/coronary stenting, or stable chronic heart failure with LVEF <= 35%.

criteria.name: Qualifying Cardiac Event (Post-MI, CABG, Valve, or LVEF <= 35%)
criteria.description: Documented qualifying diagnosis: acute MI within past 12 months, CABG, heart valve surgery, PCI/stent, stable angina, or chronic heart failure with LVEF <= 35%.
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Acute myocardial infarction within the preceding 12 months

criteria.name: Physician-Prescribed Individualized Exercise Treatment Plan
criteria.description: Documented individualized treatment plan signed by treating physician detailing exercise prescription, risk factor modification, and psychosocial assessment.
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Effective for dates of service on and after February 18, 2014, CMS has determined that the evidence is sufficient to expand coverage for cardiac rehabilitation services under 42 CFR §410.49(b)(1)(vii) to beneficiaries with stable, chronic heart failure, defined as patients with left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or less and New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II to IV symptoms despite being on optimal heart failure therapy for at least six weeks.

criteria.name: Unstable High-Risk Cardiac Condition Exclusion
criteria.description: Patients with decompensated heart failure, unstable angina, critical aortic stenosis, or severe uncontrolled ventricular arrhythmias.
criteria.clinical_intent: Exclude acute unstable states unsafe for exercise rehabilitation
criteria.source_text_excerpt: Effective for dates of service on and after February 18, 2014, CMS has determined that the evidence is sufficient to expand coverage for cardiac rehabilitation services under 42 CFR §410.49(b)(1)(vii) to beneficiaries with stable, chronic heart failure, defined as patients with left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or less and New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II to IV symptoms despite being on optimal heart failure therapy for at least six weeks.
